name: IndexSignal – SEO Index Monitor for Google
author: fastindexing

sections.description:
IndexSignal is a URL indexing and SEO monitoring plugin for WordPress and WooCommerce. It finds pages missing from search, checks technical indexability, starts eligible indexing workflows only after confirmation, and monitors saved status evidence through Day 14.

IndexSignal is an independent plugin and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google.

IndexSignal starts with private local WordPress discovery, then connects one WordPress subsite to an account only when online checks begin.

IndexSignal includes:

  • Account-free local sitemap and content discovery.
  • Secure authorization for existing and new accounts when online checks begin.
  • Verified WordPress installation and scoped installation token.
  • Posts, pages, WooCommerce products, product categories, and same-host multilingual sitemap discovery.
  • A one-time allowance of up to 200 initial URL checks, kept separate from the 200-credit trial indexing balance.
  • Local indexability analysis, Live Scan, and a basic index status check.
  • Server-calculated prices for factual checks, Basic indexing, Refund-Protected Credit-Back, and card-funded Money-Back.
  • Explicit credit confirmation before a workflow starts.
  • Check and indexing history with a D0, D5, D7, D10, and D14 monitoring timeline.
  • Native actions in Posts, Pages, Products, Gutenberg, the Classic Editor, bulk actions, and the WordPress admin bar.
  • Credit packages, quantities, exact shortfall recommendations, and secure Stripe return handling inside WordPress.
  • English and complete German (de_DE) interface text.

Google and Supabase tokens are never stored in WordPress. Network Activate is not supported; activate and connect each subsite separately.

IndexSignal uses the FastIndexing.io hosted service. The plugin performs local discovery before connection. After an administrator explicitly connects and continues, it sends the verified site URL, selected public URLs, local indexability signals, and requested actions to FastIndexing.io. Stripe checkout, optional Google authorization, remote URL checks, indexing workflows, monitoring, reports, and notifications run outside WordPress.

Privacy Policy: https://fastindexing.io/privacy
Terms: https://fastindexing.io/terms
Support: support@fastindexing.io
sections.installation:
1. Upload the indexsignal-seo-index-monitor-for-google directory to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate IndexSignal on one WordPress site.
  3. Open IndexSignal in wp-admin and run the private local site scan.
  4. Continue with an existing account or create a passwordless free account, then authorize the site.
  5. The initial Live Scan and index-status checks resume automatically in WordPress.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin store my Google token?

No. Google authorization and tokens stay in the hosted service infrastructure.

Can I Network Activate IndexSignal on multisite?

No. Per-subsite activation is supported; Network Activate is explicitly blocked.

Is an out-of-stock WooCommerce product blocked?

No. Stock status is informational. Private, catalog-hidden, noindex, or non-canonical states may block or warn.

Does the plugin automatically spend credits?

No. Local discovery is free and private. Every paid check or indexing workflow shows the current price and exclusions before the administrator confirms it.

Does IndexSignal guarantee Google indexing?

No. Google makes every indexing decision. IndexSignal checks technical eligibility, submits eligible URLs through the applicable workflow, monitors saved results, and applies Credit-Back or Money-Back terms only where they are explicitly shown before confirmation.

Is Google Search Console required?

No. Google Search Console is optional. You can connect and use the available checks and workflows without giving WordPress access to your Google credentials.

What happens when I disconnect?

The installation token is revoked on the hosted service and removed from WordPress. Account billing records and remote reports remain available until separately deleted according to the account controls and retention policy.
sections.changelog:
0.1.3

  • Add complete German (de_DE) localization and make the Gutenberg sidebar strings translatable.
  • Refresh the WordPress.org banner and animated plugin icon for a clearer directory presentation.
  • Polish public copy, onboarding terminology, and the IndexSignal brand label without changing the existing connection or credit logic.

0.1.2

  • Rename the WordPress plugin to IndexSignal and align the package, text domain, directory artwork, and documentation with the reserved WordPress.org permalink.
  • Preserve existing local settings, connection tokens, capabilities, and API protocol identifiers during the display-name migration.

0.1.1

  • Preserve all WordPress core and third-party admin notices instead of hiding or removing them.
  • Replace the post-activation redirect with a native plugin-row action.
  • Validate the one-time site-verification challenge in the REST permission callback.
  • Clarify the independent relationship with Google in the plugin name and documentation.

0.1.0

  • Prepare the first public WordPress.org release with a clean Plugin Check baseline.
  • Preserve the independent WordPress account flow while sharing the service account and website with the web dashboard.
  • Use the production Resend transactional-email provider while keeping the MailerSend rollback path.
  • Keep the immediate saved dashboard render, native WordPress Dashboard widget, admin-bar status, and direct per-page actions.
